English_source_gate: No English discrepancy established for these nine bounded labels. If review identifies a source defect, correct canonical English first, flag every affected locale, then review locales individually. No source correction or translation is implemented here.

rows.consumer_context: PaintTool.ERASER label, rendered by ToolButton and tool options/help. PaintDocument.paint selects background colour for erasing, not transparency.
rows.linguistic_rationale: The teaching source explicitly identifies this exact word as eraser. In this app it names a background-colour painting tool, not a promise of transparent deletion. The short noun does not contradict that behaviour; the separate hint explains background colour. Do not replace it with pencil based on a cross-language false friend.

confidence.basis: AI author assessment, not calibrated probability or native-speaker certification

rows.independent_check_question: Check ordinary contemporary UI familiarity; no spelling replacement is justified by the recovered lexical evidence.

rows.consumer_context: PaintTool.PENCIL label. The drawing implementation uses adjustable document.pencilWidth (1–100), square cap and no antialiasing. Current hint already describes adjustable Width; resource identifier is historical, not the English sentence.
rows.meaning_assessment: Pencil (also a word associated with lead).
rows.linguistic_rationale: The drawing-tool noun is appropriate for the crisp, non-antialiased stroke. Adjustable width does not make the pencil metaphor false. Current English hint already states Width 1–100; its historical one-pixel identifier is not a source-text defect.

confidence.basis: AI author assessment, not calibrated probability or native-speaker certification

rows.independent_check_question: Confirm normal software-tool register, without adding a one-pixel restriction.

rows.consumer_context: PaintTool.TEXT label, opens text placement/style flow. Distinguish the drawing text tool from generic prose/content.
rows.linguistic_rationale: A noun naming the tool that places and styles written text fits the current consumer. It is not a document-reading command or the name of a specific font.

confidence.basis: AI author assessment, not calibrated probability or native-speaker certification

rows.independent_check_question: No correction proposed; verify short tool-label idiom.

rows.consumer_context: AdvancedColourDialog tab selects mode0, showing basic/saved colour swatches, not a general shelf or toolbar. Review existing wording in this exact colour-selection sense without presuming it is wrong.
rows.meaning_assessment: Shelf / storage surface; potentially an inherited software-palette metaphor.
rows.linguistic_rationale: The current mode contains basic and saved colour swatches. The existing noun does not identify colours and risks sounding like a general shelf. Propose a descriptive colour-collection label rather than asserting an unsupported standard palette equivalent. This is an author-composed contextual proposal, not an attested complete dictionary phrase. The possibility that the current shelf metaphor is established remains open.

confidence.basis: AI author assessment, not calibrated probability or native-speaker certification

rows.independent_check_question: Assess whether the complete proposed phrase is idiomatic for selectable basic/saved colour swatches and better than established Amharic software terminology. Do not accept from component dictionary matches alone.

rows.consumer_context: TextStyleDialog heading immediately before TextPreview; update() displays the edited sample with size/font/colour/direction. It is a text-style preview, not save/export preview.
rows.linguistic_rationale: The heading introduces a live sample of text styling. It does not assert print fidelity, export output or saving. The glossary has a closely corresponding spelling with እ rather than current ዕ; this alone is insufficient reason for orthographic churn.

confidence.basis: AI author assessment, not calibrated probability or native-speaker certification

rows.independent_check_question: Check contemporary spelling preference independently if desired; no semantic defect established.

rows.consumer_context: EditIcon.PLUS label/content description; zoom_in action calls paintCanvas.zoomStep(1.5f). Changes viewport magnification, not image dimensions.

exact_direct_references.code: enum class EditIcon(private val labelId: Int) { SAVE(R.string.ui_save), FIT(R.string.ui_fit_entire_canvas_in_view), UNDO(R.string.ui_undo), REDO(R.string.ui_redo), CUT(R.string.ui_cut), COPY(R.string.ui_copy), PASTE(R.string.ui_paste), MINUS(R.string.ui_zoom_out), PLUS(R.string.ui_zoom_in), SELECT_ALL(R.string.ui_select_all), SIDEBAR(R.string.ui_toggle_toolbox);

rows.linguistic_rationale: This nominal label describes increasing apparent canvas magnification and is directionally correct for the plus action. It does not explicitly promise document resizing. A glossary imperative equivalent exists, but changing a clear paired noun label solely to match English imperative grammar is not necessary.

confidence.basis: AI author assessment, not calibrated probability or native-speaker certification

rows.independent_check_question: Check the near/far pair together for clear action-label and accessibility idiom; lexical alternatives are not automatic corrections.

rows.consumer_context: EditIcon.MINUS label/content description; zoom_out action calls paintCanvas.zoomStep(1/1.5f). Changes viewport magnification, not image dimensions.

exact_direct_references.code: enum class EditIcon(private val labelId: Int) { SAVE(R.string.ui_save), FIT(R.string.ui_fit_entire_canvas_in_view), UNDO(R.string.ui_undo), REDO(R.string.ui_redo), CUT(R.string.ui_cut), COPY(R.string.ui_copy), PASTE(R.string.ui_paste), MINUS(R.string.ui_zoom_out), PLUS(R.string.ui_zoom_in), SELECT_ALL(R.string.ui_select_all), SIDEBAR(R.string.ui_toggle_toolbox);

rows.linguistic_rationale: This is the counterpart to near view and correctly describes reducing apparent magnification. The code changes the viewport, not image dimensions. Retain the coherent pair rather than silently substituting a generic shrink command.

confidence.basis: AI author assessment, not calibrated probability or native-speaker certification

rows.independent_check_question: Check with Zoom in as one paired UI convention; no runtime or screen-reader execution was performed.

rows.consumer_context: TextStyleDialog text_direction spinner first option maps to TextDirection.HORIZONTAL; not a horizontal flip or page-orientation command. Existing terminal punctuation needs linguistic review in an option list, not automatic deletion.
rows.meaning_assessment: Horizontal, followed by Ethiopic introductory punctuation (፦).
rows.linguistic_rationale: The directional word fits the horizontal text-flow option. The terminal punctuation is unnecessary for a standalone spinner option, which introduces no following value. Removing it is optional UI polish, not a meaning correction or evidence that the current word is wrong. A different glossary noun is not grounds to replace the current direction word.

confidence.basis: AI author assessment, not calibrated probability or native-speaker certification

rows.independent_check_question: Decide whether punctuation omission is preferable in this option list; keep separate from the substantive Palette proposal.

rows.consumer_context: ToolCategory.SELECTION groups rectangle/lasso selection; also EditGroup.SELECTION label. ToolCategoryButton composes category and selected-tool labels in accessibility text. This is image-area selection, not choosing a menu option.
rows.linguistic_rationale: The category groups rectangular and lasso image-area tools; the broad selection noun is usable in that disambiguating context. Its other choice/election senses do not establish an error. This review covers the noun only, not the mixed-language expanded/collapsed accessibility templates or the untranslated tool names.

confidence.basis: AI author assessment, not calibrated probability or native-speaker certification

rows.independent_check_question: Check image-editing category idiom; do not treat this as acceptance of complete composed accessibility announcements.
